title: Vendor Training Data Origin and Risk Declaration (Template)
content:
Purpose:
This template is intended for use during vendor onboarding and periodic reassessments where a third party supplies training data (or derivative datasets) used to train, fine-tune, or validate generative models. It captures declarative statements from the vendor about the provenance, licensing, privacy characteristics, and identified risks of the datasets supplied, and lists the evidence the vendor must provide for verification. The goal is to create a concise, auditable record that feeds into Redwood’s ingestion risk scoring and contractual controls.

Scope:
Applies to any external supplier or partner that provides non-trivial datasets (>= 10,000 records or >1GB) used directly for training/fine-tuning or as part of any data augmentation pipeline that may influence model outputs delivered to Redwood customers. Not intended for small sample test sets provided for API compatibility checks.

Instructions to Vendor (summary):
- Complete the declaration sections below for each dataset package delivered.
- Attach required evidence items (hash manifests, license texts, sample records with redaction applied, dataset collection logs).
- If any question is answered "Unknown" or "No", provide an explanatory note in the Evidence & Comments box.
- Provide a named technical contact and legal contact for follow-up.

Section A — Dataset Identifier and Basic Metadata
1. Dataset package name (vendor-provided identifier):____________________
2. Internal dataset ID (if any):____________________
3. Delivery date (YYYY-MM-DD):____________________
4. Primary use-case claimed:____________________
5. Total size (GB) and record count:____________________
6. Data types included (select all that apply): text | images | audio | video | code | structured PII | other (describe)
7. Languages represented (top 3 by volume):____________________

Section B — Provenance and Collection Methodology (attestation)
Please answer for each dataset package delivered. Each response should be one of: Yes / No / Unknown, with short explanatory notes where applicable.
1. We collected this data directly from the original data subjects (first-party collection).  Yes / No / Unknown. Evidence required if Yes: collection form template, consent text, timestamps and retention policy.
2. We acquired the dataset from a licensed third party (broker, aggregator) with written license/assignment rights.  Yes / No / Unknown. Evidence required if Yes: signed license or purchase order, chain-of-custody email trail.
3. The dataset includes data scraped from public websites.  Yes / No / Unknown. Evidence required if Yes: list of source domains, robots.txt compliance check, scraping policy and archive of scrape timestamps.
4. The dataset contains content labeled as copyrighted (e.g., books, newspapers, proprietary code).  Yes / No / Unknown. Evidence required if Yes: list of copyrighted sources and license terms.
5. Any subset of the dataset is derived from other datasets (derivative works, synthetic augmentation, translations).  Yes / No / Unknown. Evidence required if Yes: parent dataset identifiers and transformation scripts.

Section C — Licensing, Rights, and Restrictions
1. Vendor asserts it holds sufficient rights to provide Redwood with a perpetual, worldwide, sublicensable license to use the dataset for training and inference.  Yes / No / Unknown. If No/Unknown, describe restrictions.
2. Attach the license text(s) that apply to the dataset. Provide a short summary of any attribution, share-alike, or redistribution restrictions.
3. Are there any contractual obligations requiring notification before model distribution or commercial use?  Yes / No / Unknown.
4. Are there export-control or embargo restrictions relevant to the dataset?  Yes / No / Unknown.

Section D — Personal Data and Sensitive Content
1. Does the dataset include personal data (as defined by GDPR/CCPA: names, identifiers, contact info, health, financial, etc.)?  Yes / No / Unknown. If Yes, estimate percentage of records containing personal data and provide sample redacted records.
2. Does the dataset include special category data (e.g., health, biometric, racial/ethnic data)?  Yes / No / Unknown. If Yes, provide justification for lawful basis and additional safeguards.
3. Does the dataset include minors’ data?  Yes / No / Unknown. If Yes, provide consent evidence or lawful processing basis.
4. Does the dataset include content likely to generate high-risk outputs (medical, legal, regulated financial advice)?  Yes / No / Unknown. If Yes, describe mitigation steps during labeling or model training (filtering, curated prompts, classifier-based exclusion).

Section E — Data Quality, Labeling, and Human Review
1. Describe the labeling processes used (crowdworkers, vendors, automated heuristics). Attach the labeling guideline used.
2. What is the inter-annotator agreement (if applicable)? Provide metrics or a sampled QA report.
3. Describe bias mitigation steps taken during collection and labeling. Attach sampling plans and class balance tables.
4. For synthetic data: describe generation method (model/seed, prompts, filtering, provenance of seed data).

Section F — Evidence Checklist (minimum required attachments)
- Dataset manifest (CSV/JSON) with per-file SHA256 hashes and file sizes.
- Representative sample of records (10–50) with PII redacted and redaction method documented.
- Licensing documents and chain-of-custody documentation.
- Collection or acquisition logs (timestamps, source URLs if applicable).
- Data handling and retention policy used by the vendor at time of collection.
- Labeling instructions and QA reports.
- Transformation scripts used for preprocessing/augmentation with versions.
- Contact details for technical and legal owners at the vendor.

Section G — Risk Indicators (vendor-attested quick flags)
Please mark Yes/No/Unknown and provide short notes. These flags map to Redwood’s risk taxonomy for initial scoring.
1. High proportion (>20%) of records contain direct identifiers.
2. Dataset includes content from paywalled or proprietary publishers where licensing is ambiguous.
3. Collection predates modern privacy notices (e.g., older than 2015) and no retrospective consent exists.
4. Evidence of scraping large consumer forums with mixed moderation.
5. Synthetic augmentation applied using a third-party foundation model without clear seed provenance.

Section H — Audit, Verification and Remedies
1. Redwood reserves the right to verify submitted evidence via remote inspection or on-prem audit. Vendor consents to reasonable requests for additional documentation.
2. If verification reveals material misrepresentation, Redwood may require mitigation (retraining, dataset removal), contract price adjustment, or termination for breach.
3. For high-risk findings Redwood will require a remediation plan and may decline the dataset for production use until cleared.

Section I — Signature and Attestation
By signing below, the vendor declares on behalf of the organization that the information provided in this document and the accompanying evidence is true, complete, and accurate to the best of their knowledge. Vendor understands that misrepresentation may constitute breach under the Master Services Agreement and may trigger contractual remedies.
Vendor legal signatory: Name: ____________________ Title: ____________________ Date: ___________
Vendor technical signatory (for evidence): Name: ____________________ Title: ____________________ Date: ___________

Appendix A — Example evidence templates (quick copy/paste)
- Hash manifest row format: file_path, sha256, size_bytes, created_ts
- Sample redaction note: replaced_email="[redacted:email]", redaction_method=token_mask_v1, redaction_script=redact_v1.py
- Chain-of-custody entry: delivery_id, from_entity, to_entity, date, auth_reference

Appendix B — Redwood internal guidance (for reviewer use only)
- Initial scoring guidance: Any "Yes" to Section D items flags review-required. Two or more high-risk flags in Section G escalate to the Security & Compliance review board.
- Quick evidence triage: Confirm presence of hash manifest and at least one collection log before reviewing sample records.
- Common remediation actions: scoped deletion of PII, substitution of licensed sources, removal of ambiguous scraped content, contractual indemnity for third-party claims.

Notes to vendor reviewers: Keep answers concise. Upload evidence as a single ZIP named <vendor>-<dataset>-evidence.zip and link the ZIP in the submission portal. If you cannot provide an item on the Evidence Checklist, state why and indicate planned remediation timeline.

Document version and change log:
- v0.1 (2024-11-07) initial draft (Anna Li).
- v0.2 (2025-02-12) added Appendix B triage notes and evidence templates (Miguel Ortega).

End of template.
